subject: general
question: Where does the Eastern Coastal Plain of India lie?

options.text: Between the Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal
Between the Gulf of Cambay and Cape Comorin

solution:
The correct answer is **__Between the Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Eastern Coastal Plains of India:

 
• **Eastern Coastal Plain is in between the Bay of Bengal in the East and the Eastern Ghats to the West.**
 
• Extending from the Subarnarekha river along the West Bengal-Odisha border to Kanniyakumari.
 
• A major part of the plains is formed as a result of the alluvial fillings of the littoral zone (relating to or on the shore of the sea or a lake) by the rivers Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Cauvery comprising some of the largest deltas. 
 
• In contrast to the West Coastal Plains, these are extensive plains with an average width of 120 km. 
 
• This plain is known as the Northern Circars between the Mahanadi and the Krishna rivers and Carnatic between the Krishna and the Cauvery rivers. The Eastern coast is divided into three categories
 
 
• Utkal coast
 
• Andhra coast
 
• Coromandel coast
